# Sirach Chapter 26 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 26 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**26:1** Blessed is the husband of a good wife; the number of his days will be doubled.

**26:2** A capable wife brings joy to her husband, and he will complete his years in peace.

**26:3** A good wife is a good portion; she is given in the lot of those who fear the LORD.

**26:4** Whether rich or poor, his heart is glad and his face is cheerful at all times.

**26:5** Three things caused my heart to fear, and a fourth made me prostrate myself: malicious slander in a city, the gathering of a mob, and a false accusation — all these are worse than death;

**26:6** but grief of heart and sorrow is a wife jealous of a rival wife, and a lashing tongue that makes everything known to all.

**26:7** An evil wife is a chafing yoke; taking hold of her is like grasping a scorpion.

**26:8** A drunken wife provokes great anger, and she will not cover her own shame.

**26:9** The unchastity of a woman shows in the way she lifts her eyes, and she can be recognized by her eyelids.

**26:10** Over a defiant daughter keep a strict watch, lest she find for herself an opportunity of looseness.

**26:11** Be on guard against her wandering eye, and do not be surprised when she sins against you.

**26:12** Like a thirsty traveler she will open her mouth, and drink from any water at hand; at every post she will sit down, and to every arrow she will open her quiver.

**26:13** The grace of a wife will delight her husband, and her wisdom will put flesh on his bones.

**26:14** A wife who keeps silence is a gift from the LORD, and there is no price for a disciplined soul.

**26:15** A modest wife has grace upon grace, and no price can be weighed against a continent soul.

**26:16** Like the sun rising on the heights of the Lord — so is the beauty of a good wife in the order of her household.

**26:17** Like the shining of the lamp on the holy lampstand — so is a beautiful face set upon a well-proportioned figure.

**26:18** Like golden pillars on silver bases — so are beautiful feet upon firm heels.

**26:19** My child, preserve the bloom of your youth in good health, and do not give your strength to strangers.

**26:20** Having sought out a fertile field throughout the whole land, sow it with your own seed, trusting in the excellence of your own offspring.

**26:21** Your offspring who will outlive you will be great, having confidence in their noble lineage.

**26:22** A hired woman is considered like spit, but a married woman is a tower of death to those who take hold of her.

**26:23** A lawless woman will be given as a portion to a lawless man, but a devout woman is given to a man who fears God.

**26:24** A shameless woman will be disgraced at every turn, but an honorable woman will be honored even by those who honor her.

**26:25** A lawless woman has no regard for shame, but a woman of honor respects her husband.

**26:26** A woman who honors her husband will be considered wise by all; but one who dishonors him in arrogance will be known by all as ungodly. A loud-voiced woman is like a trumpet sounding at every noise; and the war-man will lend an ear to a woman like that.

**26:27** Two things bring grief to my heart, and a third brings anger: a warrior suffering in poverty; men of discernment treated like rubbish; one who turns from righteousness to sin — the LORD will prepare him for the sword.

**26:28** [A merchant is scarcely free from negligence, and a shopkeeper will not be innocent of sin.]

**26:29** [Many have sinned for the sake of gain, and one who seeks to increase wealth averts his eyes.]
